instruction: Convert the spreadsheet to PDF format, save it to Desktop, and view it in Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Task requires converting Excel to PDF and viewing in Chrome. Evaluator checks file creation (50%) and Chrome tab opening (50%).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for PDF file created, 0.5 for PDF opened in Chrome tab

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all three instruction requirements: (1) spreadsheet converted to PDF, (2) PDF saved to Desktop at correct path, (3) PDF viewed in Chrome

Getter logic is correct: extracts file existence using env.controller.get_file() at the correct path (/home/user/Desktop/annual-enterprise-survey-2021-financial-year-provisional.pdf) and Chrome tabs using get_open_tabs_info()
Metric logic is correct: checks file existence (50% score) and Chrome tab URL exact matching (50% score) with strict equality comparison
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('pdf_url_pattern') without incorrectly expecting nested {'rules': {...}} structure
Partial credit scoring is semantically sound: 0.5 for PDF file creation, 0.5 for Chrome viewing - matches the two-step nature of the task
Data flow is correct: getter returns dict with file_exists (bool) and chrome_tabs (list), metric consumes them appropriately
Edge cases properly handled: metric handles missing files (file_exists=False) and empty Chrome tab lists
Expected values are semantically correct: pdf_path and pdf_url_pattern match the actual file from config (annual-enterprise-survey-2021-financial-year-provisional.xlsx -> .pdf)
Postconfig is present and appropriate: closes other windows while keeping Chrome open, ensuring Chrome tabs can be checked
URL matching uses exact equality (line 35: tab_url == pdf_url_pattern), which is strict and correct for this verification
